scope: Software and 'virtual RAM' (T0/T1): memory-efficiency software (compression/reclaim, dedup, tiering, KV-cache, right-sizing, cache-engine cost-down, software-defined memory, NVMe-as-RAM), tools for the shortage itself (price intelligence, marketplaces, provenance compliance, consumer compatibility), RAM-as-a-service on depreciated hardware, and content as a bridge. No hardware appliances (branch B). Research limits: 0 WebSearch calls were available (shared budget exhausted); evidence comes from GitHub/PyPI/AWS Price List API pages opened by D, plus Phase-1/B cross-references tagged as such.

cards.name: Memory FinOps Audit for Cloud SaaS
cards.what_it_is: A read-only web app with an AWS IAM role. It reads CUR plus CloudWatch-agent/Prometheus memory metrics across EC2 r/x/m-family, ElastiCache, RDS, K8s pods and JVM heaps. Output is a fixed-fee 'memory diet' report and a monitoring subscription, sold through AWS Marketplace to 20-500-engineer SaaS companies. The playbook levers are r->m family downsizing, K8s in-place pod resize (stable v1.35), JDK compact object headers and Redis->Valkey.
cards.why_it_could_work: AWS list prices put marginal RAM at $2.56-2.62/GiB-month, and RAM is 28-43% of the m7i/r7i list price (computed). Clusters leave about 18% of memory unused (Sysdig via KRR). Take a $40k/month EC2 bill with RAM at 30%, of which half the unused 18% is realizable: that saves about $1.1k/month, so a 25% share-of-savings fee is about $270/month. Reaching $20k MRR needs about 74 customers (d_calcs.py in D_notes).

evidence.title: AWS Price List API, EC2 us-east-1 (versions 2025-09 and 2026-10)
evidence.shows: Primary data. All 92 compared On-Demand Linux SKUs (c7i/m7i/m8g/r6i/r7g/r7i/r7iz/r8g/x2idn/u7i) had identical prices in Sep-2025 and Oct-2026. Marginal RAM computes to $2.56-2.62/GiB-month; x2idn.16xlarge (1 TiB) costs $6.669/h.

evidence.shows: In-place pod resource resize went stable in Kubernetes v1.35, so memory can be right-sized without pod restarts.

evidence.shows: Compact object headers integrated into JDK mainline (experimental, JDK 24). No savings figure on the page; 10-20% heap reduction is [UNVERIFIED-T].

cards.name: Fleet Memory-Reclaim Autopilot (TMO for on-prem)
cards.subbranch: Transparent memory compression / proactive reclaim / dedup
cards.what_it_is: A per-node agent plus web control plane. It enables and tunes upstream Linux zswap (zsmalloc + zstd/lz4), Meta-Senpai-style PSI-driven proactive reclaim via cgroup2, KSM page dedup on Proxmox/KVM hosts, and Kubernetes 1.34 LimitedSwap, with per-workload SLO guardrails and a 'GB reclaimed = $ of DRAM not bought' ledger. It is sold per node to on-prem/colo operators who buy DRAM at 2026 prices.
cards.why_it_could_work: On-prem buyers pay DRAM directly: $14-16/GB at contract, ~$32/GB street (64GB RDIMM $900-1,000 to $2,064). Take a 200-server x 512GB fleet with 20% cold memory at ~2:1 compression: it frees ~10 TB, which defers $154k (contract) to $328k (street) of DRAM. Kubernetes container swap went stable in v1.34, removing the old 'kubelet refuses swap' blocker. Meta reported 20-32% fleet memory savings from TMO [UNVERIFIED-T: paper not opened].

evidence.title: Meta Senpai README
evidence.shows: PSI plus cgroup2 memory.high proactive reclaim (TMO building block). Example: kernel-build peak fell from 804 MB to 348 MB.

evidence.shows: Kubernetes container swap (LimitedSwap) went stable in v1.34.

evidence.shows: 64GB RDIMM contract $450 (4Q25), above $900 (1Q26), possibly above $1,000 (2Q26).

cards.us_manufacturability: Pure software. Target customers' fleets sit in U.S. colos (Ashburn VA, Secaucus NJ). Builds on upstream Linux mm, Proxmox VE (KSM) and Kubernetes 1.34+.

The cloud K8s optimizers (CAST AI, ScaleOps) focus on requests and instances, not swap [ESTIMATE]. MemVerge left the field.
cards.wins_axis: Effective $/GB (usable GB per purchased GB), which defers DRAM capex
cards.buyer: Regional hosting providers, MSPs running Proxmox/KVM, on-prem Kubernetes and CI/build farms, and university HPC centers that must buy DDR5 RDIMMs at 2026 prices
cards.glut_reason: The deferred-DRAM value of the reference fleet falls from ~$154k to ~$61k at -60%. Density value remains but becomes a nice-to-have, and the price story behind the sale disappears.
cards.fatal_flaw: It is configuration of free kernel features. Sophisticated operators already do it themselves, and conservative ones fear swap latency and OOM incidents. One production incident at an early customer ends the company.
cards.founder_fit_note: Marginal. The control plane is easy for him; safe Linux memory-management tuning needs a kernel-savvy contractor or co-founder.
cards.possible: yes - production-proven at Meta/Google, and every component is upstream
cards.profitable: marginal - real savings while DRAM is expensive, but buyers can DIY and the pain halves in a glut
cards.doable_by_founder: marginal - needs a Linux-mm expert for SLO safety; the sales cycle to on-prem ops is slow

cards.name: KV-Cache Tier Integration & Tuning for Self-Hosted LLMs
cards.what_it_is: A productized integration service plus a benchmarking/monitoring dashboard. It deploys host-DRAM and NVMe KV-cache tiers (LMCache, NVIDIA Dynamo KVBM, Mooncake Store, SGLang HiCache) into mid-market vLLM/SGLang clusters and sizes the DRAM tier per workload from measured prefix-reuse rates. Recurring revenue comes from hit-rate, TTFT and $/token monitoring.
cards.why_it_could_work: Llama-3.1-70B needs 320 KiB of KV per token, so 1 TB of host DRAM ($15k at 2026 contract) holds ~3.1M reusable prefix tokens. Mooncake reports Kimi serving 75% more requests within SLO, and Dynamo claims 2x TTFT from KV-aware routing. The stacks churn fast (LMCache shipped 65 PyPI releases from May 2025 to Oct 2026; vLLM 0.32.0 came out 2026-10-18), and teams running 8-64 GPUs lack staff to keep up.

evidence.title: LMCache README
evidence.shows: Open-source KV-cache layer (CPU/SSD/remote tiers) for vLLM, integrated into NVIDIA Dynamo (Sep 2025). Development supported by Tensormesh.

evidence.shows: Free Apache-2.0 KVBM offloads KV GPU->CPU->SSD->remote. Claims 2x TTFT from KV-aware routing (Baseten).

evidence.title: Mooncake README
evidence.shows: KV-centric disaggregated serving at Kimi: 75% more requests within SLO. Integrated into vLLM, SGLang, LMCache, Dynamo and TensorRT-LLM (2026-10-10).

evidence.shows: Tensormesh, the company around LMCache, ships a hosted serverless-inference and control-plane SDK (first release 2026-04-02).

cards.time_to_first_revenue_text: 6-12 months: an integration engagement ($15-40k) with an enterprise AI team or small U.S. GPU cloud, then a monitoring retainer.
cards.us_manufacturability: Software and services. Customers' GPU clusters are in U.S. colos (Ashburn VA, NJ). Builds on Apache-2.0 LMCache, Dynamo and Mooncake.
cards.who_is_already_doing_this: Tensormesh (the LMCache creators: hosted inference plus control-plane SDK, first PyPI release 2026-04), NVIDIA (Dynamo, free), Moonshot (Mooncake), Red Hat llm-d [UNVERIFIED-T], WEKA Augmented Memory Grid, Pliops, VAST [UNVERIFIED-T], hosted inference providers (Baseten, Together, Fireworks).
cards.wins_axis: $/token and TTFT: host DRAM ($/GB) substitutes for re-computing prefill on HBM GPUs
cards.buyer: Mid-market teams self-hosting 70B-class open models on 8-64 GPUs for data-residency reasons (legal-tech, healthcare, fintech)
cards.glut_reason: A glut makes host DRAM cheaper and the KV tier more attractive. The value is GPU-hours avoided, which does not depend on DRAM prices.
cards.fatal_flaw: NVIDIA, the vLLM/SGLang maintainers and Tensormesh are turning this into defaults and SaaS, so the integration gap closes within 12-18 months. Buyers purchase GPU-infra credibility the founder does not have.
cards.founder_fit_note: Marginal. Python/K8s skills transfer, but credibility in GPU serving must be earned and the field moves weekly.
cards.possible: yes - shipping open source at Moonshot/Kimi and integrated into NVIDIA Dynamo

cards.doable_by_founder: marginal - needs GPU access for benchmarking and deep inference-stack knowledge

cards.name: Cache-Tier Cost-Down: Redis -> Valkey/Dragonfly Sizing
cards.what_it_is: A sizing tool that ingests Redis INFO/MEMORY STATS, keyspace samples and ElastiCache bills, and models savings from engine migration (Redis OSS -> Valkey on ElastiCache, or self-hosted Dragonfly), encoding changes and node downsizing. It is sold as a fixed-fee migration plan plus an optional memory-drift monitor.
cards.why_it_could_work: Verified AWS list prices for cache.r7g.large: Redis OSS $0.219/h vs Valkey $0.1752/h (-20%). New Redis OSS Extended Support SKUs add $0.175/h (Yr1-2) or $0.35/h (Yr3). A 50-node fleet goes from ~$14.4k/month (Redis + extended support) to ~$6.4k/month on Valkey (-56%). Dragonfly's vendor test claims ~30% less memory idle and no ~3x snapshot spike.

cards.why_it_could_work: Pooling recovers stranded memory (Azure's Pond work reported ~7-9% DRAM savings [UNVERIFIED-T]), and each stranded GB is worth 4x more in 2026. CXL switches (XConn, Astera Labs) are shipping in pilots.

cards.name: NVMe-as-RAM Virtual Memory Software (IMDT/ScaleMP revival, tempting, dead)
cards.what_it_is: A thin hypervisor or kernel layer that presents NVMe SSDs as system RAM (the Intel Memory Drive Technology / ScaleMP vSMP MemoryONE approach), so a server with 256GB DRAM plus 4TB NVMe shows 4TB of 'memory'. It would be sold as a per-server license.
cards.why_it_could_work: NAND $/GB is a small fraction of DRAM even after its own 2026 rise, NAND is forecast to turn to surplus in 2H27 (TrendForce via p1), and the arbitrage looks enormous on paper.

cards.why_it_could_work: A 4x price spike turns stranded inventory into cash, and liquidity is fragmented among phone-and-email brokers. Spot is thin and broker-driven, and DDR4 spot hit a record $47.04.

cards.name: DIMM Provenance Scanner (Sec. 5949 CXMT/YMTC audit)
cards.what_it_is: An open-core Linux/Windows agent plus web dashboard. It reads every installed DIMM's SPD EEPROM (module-manufacturer JEP106 ID, DRAM-die manufacturer ID, part/serial, date code) across a server fleet or an incoming lot, flags CXMT (JEP106 0x0A11) and YMTC (0x091B) content, and produces audit-ready inventories for federal integrators ahead of the NDAA FY2023 Sec. 5949 ban (effective Dec 2027). Physical spot-confirmation would be referred to a U.S. AS6081 test lab.
cards.why_it_could_work: CXMT is becoming the marginal DRAM supplier (9.5% revenue share in 2Q26, ramping), while Sec. 5949 bars federal purchases of products containing CXMT/YMTC/SMIC chips from Dec 2027. JEP106 IDs are public (memtest86+ carries JEP106BP, Sep 2026), and SPD reading is solved code (memtest86+, i2c-tools decode-dimms). Integrators need fleet-scale evidence, not one-off decaps.

evidence.title: memtest86+ JEP106 table
evidence.shows: Based on JEP106BP (Sep 2026): CXMT = 0x0A11, YMTC = 0x091B.

evidence.title: memtest86+ SPD decoder
evidence.shows: Reads the manufacturer JEP106 ID from SPD (DDR5 bytes 512-513, DDR4 bytes 320-321) plus date code and part number.

evidence.title: XenoSpectrum on federal China-memory ban (via p1-backend)
evidence.shows: NDAA FY2023 s.5949: no federal purchases of products containing SMIC/YMTC/CXMT chips from Dec 2027.

evidence.title: Herald Corp / TrendForce DRAM share (via p1-market)
evidence.shows: CXMT at 9.5% of DRAM revenue in 2Q26.

cards.time_to_first_revenue_text: 9-15 months: a paid pilot ($10-25k) with a GSA/defense IT integrator preparing for Dec 2027, then per-node subscriptions.
cards.us_manufacturability: Pure software built in the U.S. Partners: memtest86+/i2c-tools SPD-decoding lineage (GPL, to be reimplemented cleanly) and U.S. AS6081 counterfeit-test labs for physical confirmation.
cards.who_is_already_doing_this: BOM-level risk tools (SiliconExpert, Z2Data) work on part numbers, not installed-fleet SPD [UNVERIFIED-T]. Server OEM supplier attestations (Dell, HPE), firmware supply-chain vendors (Eclypsium [UNVERIFIED-T]), and ITAD asset-inventory tools. No dedicated fleet-SPD provenance product found (search budget exhausted; unconfirmed).
cards.buyer: Federal systems integrators and GSA Schedule resellers; defense-prime IT; critical-infrastructure operators with 'no-China-memory' policies
cards.glut_reason: Demand comes from law (Dec 2027), not price. A CXMT-led glut increases CXMT content in the channel and the need to detect it.
cards.fatal_flaw: SPD is writable and the DRAM-manufacturer field is set by the module maker, so it can be blank or spoofed: software can triage but not prove provenance. And if the FAR rule accepts supplier attestations or excludes subcomponents, nobody pays for scanning.
cards.founder_fit_note: Yes. Agent plus dashboard is his skill set, and the domain is learnable from JEDEC docs. Federal sales need a channel partner.
cards.possible: yes - SPD decode is mature; mapping JEP106 to CXMT is trivial
cards.profitable: marginal - hinges on the FAR rule scope and on integrators paying rather than self-attesting
cards.doable_by_founder: yes - T0, software-only; the first customer is the hard part

cards.name: Embedded RAM-Diet Profiler for Small Hardware OEMs
cards.what_it_is: A CLI plus web report that profiles the real memory footprint of an embedded Linux/Yocto/Android product image under worst-case load (PSS via smem, cgroup peaks, zram headroom). It produces an engineering case for dropping one LPDDR4/DDR4 density step (e.g., 2GB->1GB) or enabling zram, priced per product line for small OEMs whose BOMs ballooned in 2026.
cards.why_it_could_work: LPDDR4X rose +70-75% QoQ in 2Q26, and mobile LTAs signed near $21/GB. At 20k units/year x 1GB saved x $8-21/GB, a product line saves $160k-420k/year in BOM cost. zram's expected ~2:1 compression gives headroom without new silicon.

cards.who_is_already_doing_this: Embedded consultancies (Bootlin, Witekio, Toradex services) [UNVERIFIED-T], SoM vendor application engineers, Yocto buildhistory and smem (free), device-observability SaaS (Memfault [UNVERIFIED-T]).
cards.wins_axis: $/unit BOM (fewer GB of DRAM per device)
cards.buyer: Hardware product managers at U.S. industrial, IoT and medical-device OEMs shipping 5k-200k units/year
cards.glut_reason: At glut prices a 1GB step saves ~$2.5/unit, below the cost of re-spin and re-qualification, so demand evaporates.
cards.fatal_flaw: Dropping a density step means board re-spin, re-qualification and (for medical) regulatory re-validation that cost more than a year of savings. Embedded engineers decide, and they rarely buy SaaS from non-engineers.
